abstract: Before an AI agent takes on a paid job, someone has to judge whether it is likely to succeed. We test whether frontier language models can make this call before any attempt. We propose PAYWORTHY which contains 1{,}494 real freelance job postings, sampled from 18.8M postings made between 2020 and 2026 on a freelancing platform. An agent attempts each job from the posting alone in a single run, and an LLM judge acting as the client decides whether to accept the work. We ask 18 models to forecast how likely the agent is to succeed and measure how well each model's forecasts rank the accepted jobs above the rejected ones (AUC, where 0.5 is a random ranking). The answer depends on how the agent is described. Told what the agent cannot do, every model ranks the jobs well (AUC 0.66--0.86). Told instead that it is a generic agent with a browser and code execution, the same models rank the same jobs about as well as a random ordering (0.45--0.56). These results hold under judges from four other model families (Claude, GLM, Kimi and Qwen), and the informed forecasts also rank the verdicts of two human raters.   Code is available at https://github.com/upwork/Payworthy

ob.tldr: 基于1,494个真实自由职业岗位，比较18个模型在AI智能体接单前预测任务完成可能性的能力。明确描述智能体能力边界时，AUC达0.66—0.86；仅描述浏览器和代码执行功能时，表现接近随机，且结论可跨模型家族复现。

title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?
title_zh: PAYWORTHY：LLM能否预测AI智能体将完成哪些自由职业任务？
